_about: Module 2 outline for the Summary Writer. Headings follow ICH M4 (organisation), M4Q(R1), M4S and M4E(R2); the guidance lines are paraphrased, not quoted. Word targets: about 450 words a page.

headings.title: Introduction
headings.guide: One page. Name the product (proprietary name and INN), its pharmacological class and how it works, the dosage form, strengths and route, and the indication proposed. Say what this application covers.

headings.title: Introduction
headings.guide: Proprietary name, INN, company, dosage form, strengths, route and proposed indication, in a few lines.

headings.title: S.1 General Information
headings.guide: Nomenclature, structure (with formula and molecular weight) and the general properties that matter for the product: solubility, polymorphism, pKa.

headings.title: S.2 Manufacture
headings.guide: Name and address of each drug substance manufacturer; a short description of the process and its controls; the materials, critical steps and process validation or evaluation in summary; the development history that matters.

headings.title: S.3 Characterisation
headings.guide: How the structure was confirmed, and a summary of the impurities: their origin, which are specified, and the limits.

headings.title: S.4 Control of Drug Substance
headings.guide: The specification as a table (test, method, limit), a summary of the analytical procedures and their validation, the batch analyses, and why the specification is justified.

headings.title: S.5 Reference Standards or Materials
headings.guide: The reference standards used and how they were qualified.

headings.title: S.6 Container Closure System
headings.guide: The container in which the drug substance is stored and shipped, and why it is suitable.

headings.title: S.7 Stability
headings.guide: The studies done (conditions, batches, time points), the results and the proposed retest period or shelf life, and the commitment for ongoing studies.

headings.title: P.1 Description and Composition of the Drug Product
headings.guide: The dosage form, the strengths, and the composition of each strength with the function of each component.

headings.title: P.2 Pharmaceutical Development
headings.guide: How the formulation and process were developed: the drug substance and excipient choices, critical quality attributes, the manufacturing process development and the container closure choice.

headings.title: P.3 Manufacture
headings.guide: Each manufacturer and its responsibilities, the batch formula, a flow of the process with in-process controls, and the process validation summary.

headings.title: P.4 Control of Excipients
headings.guide: The excipient standards (pharmacopoeial or in-house) and anything novel or of animal origin.

headings.title: P.5 Control of Drug Product
headings.guide: The specification as a table, the analytical procedures and their validation in summary, the batch analyses, the impurities, and the justification of the specification.

headings.title: P.6 Reference Standards or Materials
headings.guide: Reference standards used for the drug product tests, if different from S.5.

headings.title: P.7 Container Closure System
headings.guide: The packaging for each presentation, its materials, and why it suits the product.

headings.title: P.8 Stability
headings.guide: The stability studies (conditions, batches, time points), the results, the proposed shelf life and storage, and the post-approval stability commitment. Say how the shelf life is supported, including any extrapolation.

headings.title: A Appendices
headings.guide: Facilities and equipment, adventitious agents safety evaluation and novel excipients, where they apply (mostly biologics).

headings.title: R Regional Information
headings.guide: Information the region asks for, such as executed batch records in the US or the medical device for a combination product in the EU.
